title: Neural Network Imitation of Model Predictive Control for RLC Circuit Voltage Regulation:  A Simulation Case Study with PID Control Comparison
content: Automated control systems form a vital aspect in the continued safe operation of any industrial facility. At present, the PID algorithm forms the basis of more than 95% of industrial automated control systems. However, classical PIDs are known to have deficiencies when dealing modern plants dynamic characteristics. Model Predictive Controllers (MPC) have been offered as one of the solutions to overcome the shortcomings of the traditional PID controllers. However, MPCs are computationally demanding for the micro-second level sampling rates, typical of power converters and voltage regulators. One of the possible solutions being investigated, in this regard is the deployment of a feed-forward neural network trained to imitate the control policy of the MPC. In this paper, this approach is discussed, taking into account a voltage regulator with a continuous time series linear RLC plant with a measurable load-current disturbance. The plant was subjected to a set of target voltages within 5-24 V and load current disturbances between 0-1 A and a neural network was trained with the MPC’s control action. Thereafter the trained NN controller was deployed for closed loop validation in a Simulink environment. The results obtained, indicated that the neural network behavioral clone retained most of the qualitative benefits of the MPC at a much smaller computational cost. Also, NN controller was compared with a tuned and back-calculation windup enabled PID regulator and a PID regulator provided with a feed-forward measurement of the load current disturbance.
